fields.meta_title: Free Emergency Contact Form Builder | Emergent
fields.meta_description: Build an emergency contact form that requires a backup number, keeps medical notes apart and asks people to reconfirm every year.
fields.h1: Build an Emergency Contact Form That Stays Current
fields.hero_description: Describe who fills it in and who reads it in a hurry. Emergent builds the emergency contact form and the records behind it. A yearly reminder keeps every phone number current.
fields.features_heading: What a Current Contact Record Needs
fields.features_subheading: A printed sheet goes stale in the filing cabinet. These six pieces keep a working number in reach when someone has to call.
fields.feature_1:
A backup contact the form insists on

Require a second person with a different phone number before the form submits. When the first call goes to voicemail, the caller has another name on the same screen.
fields.feature_2:
Relationship picked from a short list

Offer spouse, partner, parent, sibling, friend and other as choices instead of a blank line. Whoever makes the call knows at a glance who is likely to pick up the phone.
fields.feature_3:
Medical notes kept in their own file

Collect allergies and medications in a separate, optional section. HR or the school nurse can open it, while a shift lead sees only the names and numbers needed to call.
fields.feature_4:
A yearly check that numbers still work

Email each person a confirm link on the anniversary of their last update. Records nobody has confirmed show up on a short list for the office manager to chase by phone.
fields.feature_5:
A lookup card for whoever is on shift

Search a name on a phone and see both contacts with tap-to-call numbers. A night supervisor or a camp counselor reaches family without waiting for the office to open.
fields.feature_6:
Code you can take with you

Export the full codebase to your GitHub repository to connect the records to your HR system or run the app on your own servers. Every line of the app belongs to you.
fields.why_description: A fillable PDF records the names once and goes in a drawer. Nobody learns the number changed until the call fails.

fields.usecase_heading: Who Keeps Emergency Contacts on File
fields.tab_content_1:
Two contacts on file before the first shift

Granite Freight hires forklift drivers for its Reno warehouse. Each new hire opens the form on a phone at orientation and adds the person to call first and a backup. The form will not submit until the backup has a different phone number. Allergies and medications are optional and go to a file only HR can open.
fields.tab_content_2:
Allergies and pickup names on the classroom tablet

At Little Oaks Learning Center, parents complete enrollment on a phone, listing emergency contacts, everyone allowed to collect their child and any allergy. The Toddler Room tablet shows each child as a card. When a grandmother arrives at pickup, the teacher sees her name and the peanut allergy together.
fields.tab_content_3:
Once a year, every family checks its numbers

Maple Ridge Senior Living asks each resident's family to confirm their phone numbers every year. Any record not confirmed in 12 months gets an email with a confirm link. The front desk calls anyone with no reply in 7 days.
fields.tab_content_4:
Cabin 4 has three campers with no backup

Six days before arrival, the director of Pine Hollow Camp checks contacts cabin by cabin. Every camper needs two people the camp can call. Cabin 4 has three campers with no backup listed, and those families get an email asking for one before the bus leaves.

fields.howto_title: How to Create an Emergency Contact Form
fields.howto_description: Work out who reads the record, and how often it gets checked, before anything else.
fields.howto_step_2_title: 02 Ask for two people, not one
fields.howto_step_4_title: 04 Pick a date each year to confirm
fields.howto_step_1_des: Picture the person making the call, such as a night supervisor or a teacher at pickup. List what they need on one screen. Names, relationships and phone numbers come first, and everything else can sit a tap away.
fields.howto_step_2_des: Require a primary and a backup contact, each with a mobile number. Ask that the backup lives somewhere else or keeps different hours. A spouse and a sibling across town cover more of the day than two people in one house.
fields.howto_step_3_des: Put allergies, medications and conditions in an optional section of their own. Decide who may open it, for example HR or the school nurse. Leave it off the lookup screen that supervisors use.
fields.howto_step_4_des: Choose when every record gets checked, such as the hire anniversary or the first week of school. Write the reminder email and set how long people have to answer. Name the person who phones anyone who stays silent.
fields.howto_step_5_des: Write the fields, the rules and the reminder schedule in one prompt in plain English. Emergent builds the form and the database behind it, with a lookup view for staff. Change any rule later by asking for it.
fields.howto_step_6_des: If your HR or school software has an API, connect it so new hires or enrolled children appear without retyping. Send updates back the same way. A Slack or email alert can tell the office when a record changes.
fields.howto_step_7_title: 07 Fill it in as a new hire would
fields.howto_step_7_des: Open the form on a phone and try to submit it with one contact, then with the same number twice. Confirm the form stops you both times. Then look up the test record as a supervisor and place the call.

plan.angle: The live top 10 is fillable PDFs from employers and agencies (FRTIB, a hospital intake packet, a college fitness center), printable templates (eForms, AIHR, Eddy, Etsy) and builder templates (Jotform, SurveyMonkey, Fillout). Every one collects the contacts once and stops. The failure people hit is the call that goes nowhere: a number from three years ago, no backup, a teacher who cannot find the allergy. This page answers what the form needs and the relationship questions People Also Ask, then shows four places the record has to stay current and reachable: new hires, a daycare classroom, a senior living community and a summer camp.
tab_stories: A new hire at a warehouse fills in the form on a phone during onboarding, and it will not submit until a second contact with a different phone number is on file; medical notes go to a separate HR-only record.
A parent enrolling a child at a daycare lists two emergency contacts, the people allowed to pick up and a peanut allergy, and the classroom tablet shows that card to the teacher.
A senior living community emails each resident's family once a year to confirm their numbers, and anyone not confirmed in 12 months gets a reminder from the front desk.
A summer camp director checks contacts cabin by cabin before arrival day and sees three campers in Cabin 4 with no second number, so those families get an email.

claims_to_source: Under the ADA, medical information an employer collects about an employee must be kept on separate forms, in a separate confidential medical file
On iPhone, emergency contacts and their relationship are added in the Medical ID section of the Health app, which first responders can see from the Lock screen
On Android, emergency contacts are added in the Safety app under Your info
